relevance_note: The paper describes identifiable patients with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase (SSADH) deficiency and their ALDH5A1 variants, as in '13 ALDH5A1 variants (1 splicing variant, 3 deletion variants and 9 missense variants) were detected in 12 probands', plus one further patient carrying a homozygous ALDH5A1 variant.
method_note: Read the paper Markdown including the converted 'Supplementary material' section; no script transcribed any table, and no table contained stacked ' / ' cells (D-31 did not apply). Individuals: the 12 patients of Supplementary Table 2 (bare numbers 1-12 in its 'ID' column, called 'patient 1', 'Patient 3', 'patient 9' in the Results text) are labelled 'Patient 1'-'Patient 12'; a thirteenth person, the 'undiagnosed patient with epilepsy and encephalatrophy' carrying homozygous c.515G > A (p.R172H), described only in the Results text, is labelled 'unnamed person 1' (label rule 6). Supplementary Table 2's columns are ID | Variants | Variant type | Zygosity | Sex | Onset | Follow-up | Seizure | Intellectual disability | Communication | Motor developmental delay | Other abnormalities; its legend defines F = female, M = male, NA = not available and '-' = loss of follow-up, so NA and '-' cells are 'not reported' while the plain word 'No' was read as an explicit absence. Contradictions found: for patient 1 Supplementary Table 2 gives intellectual disability 'Below elementary-school level' while the Results text says 'her intelligence was normal', and the table gives 'Motor developmental delay: No' while the text says 'Her motor ability was moderately impaired'; both pairs are emitted as observed plus excluded rows, and the two checklist items (intellectual disability; gross or fine motor deficits) are 'not reported'. Two cohort variants are absent from Tables 1, 2 and 4 and from the 14-variant analyses: c.1344-2del (p.?) and chr:24403265-24566986del (p.?) (Supplementary Table 2 gives 'chr:24403265-24566986del (p.?)' for patient 2), so their variant class, pathogenicity and ACMG codes are 'not reported'. Supplementary Table 1 prints 'c.86-116del' and 'c.398-399del' where the rest of the paper prints 'c.85_116del' and 'c.398_399del'; Table 4 prints '﹥' where Table 1 prints '>'. The paper's variant classes are 'Missense', 'Deletion' and 'Splicing'; because the enum has no plain 'deletion' category the three 'Deletion' variants are recorded as 'other'. The transcript NM_001080.3 is printed once in the Methods for the study's ALDH5A1 sequence and is recorded on every variant row. The SNPs c.538 C > T (p.H180Y) and c.545 C > T (p.P182L) are reported as detected in patients 1 and 5 but are classified Benign/Likely Benign (BA1/BS1), so they are treated as common variants the authors dismiss as non-causal and get no variant rows. Parental testing is described only study-wide ('Sanger sequencing was performed on DNA samples from the proband and both of their parents') with no result for any individual, so no relative rows were created and inheritance/parental_testing_statement are 'not reported' for everyone; that sentence mentions parents only as a group, so no parent rows were invented. Patients 1-9 are stated to have been reported earlier ('patients 1 ~ 9 have been reported as clinical case series by us [13]'), which is recorded in publications.cites_prior_report_of_same_patients and prior_report_citation and copied into source_reference_in_review for those nine patients. 'Encephalatrophy' was read as cerebral atrophy, 'severe hyperactivity disorder' as attention problems or ADHD, and the Communication column as speech or language impairment. For patient 3 the text states 'no abnormalities in epilepsy, psychiatric status, or motor function'; the epilepsy and motor parts are used for those checklist items, while the broad 'psychiatric status' wording is recorded only as the paper's own phrase and is not mapped to narrower checklist items. Note on whitespace: in Table 1 and in some Results sentences the paper prints variant strings with thin (U+2009) or non-breaking spaces around '>' and after the position number, so a few spans are shorter fragments taken from those same rows rather than the full variant string. Functional evidence for each variant comes from the Table 1 enzyme-activity column and from the per-variant sentences in the Results (Fig. 3 and Fig. 4 are images).
